reviews.title: Misleading Advertising and Limited Identification Tools
reviews.text:
I purchased Plant Parent hoping for two main features: reliable plant care guidance and easy plant identification. While the app does provide basic care instructions, it unfortunately falls short of the expectations set by its advertising.

One of my biggest disappointments is that there is no straightforward option to simply scan a plant and identify what it is. Instead, the app seems heavily focused on diagnosing problems and assessing plant health. There are many situations where users already have a healthy plant and simply want to know its species, care requirements, or growing habits. Having to navigate through a diagnosis-oriented process feels unnecessarily cumbersome and does not align with what many plant owners are looking for.

The care information provided is helpful but fairly general and not significantly different from what can be found through a quick online search. Based on the marketing materials, I expected more detailed, personalized, and comprehensive guidance. The app’s promotional content suggests a more robust plant-identification and plant-management experience than what is actually delivered.

The user interface is attractive and easy to navigate, and I appreciate the effort to consolidate plant care tools into one platform. However, the lack of a dedicated plant identification feature and the mismatch between the advertised capabilities and the actual user experience make it difficult for me to fully recommend the app.

reviews.title: Dodgy membership practices
reviews.text:
So I got a new phone and realised I would have to sign up as a member to transfer all my plant data from my old one. No problem, 7 day free trial, all good. I hadn’t signed up yet because I was testing a couple of other apps out.

So everything goes fine, my plants come up on my phone but then I realise that on my new phone it’s telling me I should have watered some of my plants three days ago… bit odd, so I checked the care tab for the plants and the watering routine had changed from every 10 days to every 7 days.

I checked my other plants and it turned out all the succulents watering times had also changed to be further apart… 

Given that these changes happened after I signed up for membership, can I assume that plant parent was giving me information that wasn’t giving the proper care to my plants?

Furthermore the first impulse point when you look at the membership sign up claims “Premium members are 2.6x more likely to keep their plants happy” given that the information I’m now getting is more likely to keep my plants happy, (possibly 2.6x) I do wonder where they got that figure from.

I’ve really enjoyed using the app and would love to be shown that it’s just a mistake. If it isn’t, I’m not sure how I feel about paying a company that gives misleading information to its customers in the hopes of making more money.

reviews.title: Killed my plant
reviews.text:
AVOID! This app is terrible. It told me when to water my plants after putting all the correct information in that it asked for. After one month my plant died by under watering! I asked for a refund from Apple as I had to pay for a year’s subscription - there was no trial - and they declined twice! I have now paid £30 for absolutely nothing and for the pleasure of having my plant died. I could have done that myself for free 🤬

UPDATE: following the developer reply I tried again to get a refund but they won’t give one. I apparently am not eligible for a refund despite the app not working. Not only have I wasted money on this app but it is responsible for killing my plant which I have had to pay to replace. This feels like a total scam and against my consumer rights. 
I can’t send the photos the developer wants, the plant died weeks ago so I threw it away. What a joke!
Don’t waste your money, you’ll never get it back.

reviews.title: Falsely advertising family sharing
reviews.text:
This is listed as a family sharing app. It is not, however. The description of family sharing, says that you can share with up to five family members without additional cost. This is not true. To share with additional family members you have to buy a family subscription for an additional cost. I did a 7 day free trial to see if I thought my son would like it and be able to use it. When the trial was over I let it do the purchase thinking we’d be able to add it to his device through family sharing. He can’t access it, however. When I reached out to customer support, I’m pretty sure I got an chatbot especially since after several messages back and forth, it ended up sending me the exact same message later in the conversation that it had at the beginning with instructions on how to sign in on another device with my Apple ID. 
Whether it was a chatbot or a person, it seemed to be telling me I needed to buy the family plan. Very frustrating since nobody else in the family will use it. I may have been willing to purchase this for multiple years, but given the customer service, I don’t know that that will be happening.
